candidate.selection_reason: user-provided file paths -> applies escaping -> used in git add command construction
candidate.source_summary: files parameter passed to commit function, originates from file stream processing JSON package files in index.js
candidate.sink_summary: Escaped files string concatenated into shell command: cp.exec(gitApp + " add " + files, gitExtra, done) on line 55
candidate.guard_summary: escapeQuotes function wraps each file path in double quotes and escapes characters ["'$`\\] with backslashes before shell command construction
candidate.risk_pattern: File paths from file system are escaped and used in shell command execution; escaping attempts to prevent command injection but may have limitations
used_variable_sources: escapeQuotes function defined in same file
candidate.context_summary: In commit function, file paths are escaped and joined with spaces, then used in 'git add' shell command via child_process.exec
unresolved_facts: Exact source of file paths in the files array - appears to come from file stream but exact origin unclear
Whether file paths could contain newlines or other problematic characters not handled by escapeQuotes
Whether the double-quote wrapping combined with backslash escaping is sufficient for all shell metacharacters
Whether there are any other callers of commit function besides index.js

target_cwe.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
target_cwe.description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component. This weakness can lead to a vulnerability in environments in which the attacker does not have direct access to the operating sy...
target_cwe.impact: code execution, data access, data modification
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements
Implement strict input validation with whitelisting

stage3_hypothesis.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
stage3_hypothesis.fit_reason: Evidence: shell command execution via cp.exec with concatenated file paths; OS command injection is a specific variant of command injection relevant to git commands.
